+---
+assignees:

+- 01M1H2RGWFM5DE6BRJFGB7YXNF

+position_ordinal: '8380'
+title: Drain the file-change journal at the end of each runCode call and post the change set
+---
+## What
+Ask 4, part 3 (UPSTREAM_ASKS.md). Drain each recording journal at the end of `MultiTool.call`, and hand the set to the host as a `.progress` `OperationEvent` whose `detail` is the JSON envelope of `FileChangeSet.encodedOperationEventDetail()`. `SandboxNoticeOutbox.swift:35` is the precedent for a post from inside this package.
+
+Change `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/MultiTool.swift`, `runSnippet(arguments:)`:
+- After `await notices?.flush()` and before the `lostRuns` check, call a new `private func postFileChanges(of bundle: RegistryBundle, through binding: RunBinding?) async`.
+- That method drains every journal of `bundle.changeJournals` in order. For each set with at least one change, and when `binding` is not `nil`, it posts:
+  ```swift
+  OperationEvent(
+      tool: binding.context.tool,
+      op: binding.context.op,
+      correlationID: binding.context.completionToken,
+      kind: .progress,
+      detail: changeSet.encodedOperationEventDetail())
+  ```
+  through `binding.context.post(_:)`. An empty set posts nothing. With no binding (a `MultiTool` called outside a session) the journal is still drained, and the set is dropped: no session can receive it. Document this on the method.
+- Put the drain on both the success path and the failure path, exactly as the notice flush is: a write that landed is a write that landed, whatever the snippet did next.
+- Order matters: the post happens before `call(arguments:)` hands its result back, so the host sees the change event before the run's terminal event. State this in the doc comment, with the same reason the notice flush gives.
+
+Update documentation:
+- `FilesCapability.init` and `MultiTool.Builder.withFiles` doc for `recordsChanges`: the recorded changes are posted at the end of each `runCode` call as a `.progress` event whose detail is the `fileChanges` envelope. Name `FileChangeSet.init(operationEventDetail:)` as the way a host reads it.
+- `FileChangeJournal.swift` header: `drain()` now has its caller.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A `MultiTool` over `.withFiles(root:recordsChanges: true)`, called under a stub session context, runs a snippet that calls `tools.files.write` once. The recorded events hold exactly one `.progress` event whose `detail` decodes with `FileChangeSet(operationEventDetail:)` to a set with one `.add` change at the written path, with `root` equal to the canonical root.
+- [ ] That event's `correlationID` is the outer run's `completionToken`.
+- [ ] That event is recorded before the run's terminal `.completed` event.
+- [ ] A snippet that calls `tools.files.patch` with three files posts ONE event carrying three changes, not three events.
+- [ ] A snippet that only reads (`tools.files.read`) posts no `fileChanges` event.
+- [ ] The same capability, not recording (`recordsChanges: false`), posts no `fileChanges` event after a write.
+- [ ] After the call returns, a second `drain()` on the capability's journal is empty (the call drained it).
+- [ ] A snippet whose write landed and that then throws still posts the `fileChanges` event.
+- [ ] The `runCode` rendered result text is unchanged by recording (the model never sees the change set).
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Add `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/FileChangeEventTests.swift`. Build the registry with `MultiTool.Builder().withFiles(root:recordsChanges:).buildRegistry()`, make a `MultiTool(registry:)`, get a context with `makeStubRun()` (`Fixtures/StubRouterFixtures.swift`), and run the snippet with `ToolContext.$current.withValue(context)` as `SandboxGlobalsTests.runSnippet` does. Read events with `recordedOperationEvents(of:ofKind:)`. Cover each acceptance criterion above with one test.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter "FileChangeEvent|FilesCapabilityTests|SandboxGlobalsTests"` and expect every test to pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+    ### research
+    - `FileChangeJournal.commit(_:through:)` posts one `.progress` event through `ToolContext.post(_:)`. `SessionOutbox.post(event:)` in Router awaits the journal write (`await journalWrite?.value`) before it returns. Thus the event is in the recorder before `MultiTool.call(arguments:)` returns, and criterion 2 needs no wait.
+    - `RunBinding.invoke` mounts each inner call with `context.mount(tool, op:as:)`. The mount forwards each event through the captured context, and `post` re-stamps the event with the outer `completionToken`.
+    - The fixtures `makeFilesRun(named:recordsChanges:)` and `runSnippet(_:over:under:)` in `Fixtures/FilesRunFixtures.swift` are the ground. `runSnippet` makes a new `MultiTool` for each call. The concurrent test must run two calls over ONE `MultiTool`, so the fixture gets an overload `runSnippet(_:through:under:)` that takes the `MultiTool`.
+    - `ReleaseGate` holds ONE waiter. Two snippets cannot both wait on it. A `Rendezvous` actor (party size 2) counts arrivals: the first arrival waits on the gate, the second arrival releases it. Only one waiter blocks. A `RendezvousTool` (standalone tool, `Builder.addTools`) lets a snippet call `await tools.rendezvous({})`.
+    - `recordedOperationEvents(of:ofKind:correlatedTo:awaiting:)` polls. The card asks for a read with no wait, so the fixture gets an overload `recordedOperationEvents(of:ofKind:correlatedTo:)` and the polling one calls it.
+    - The renderer writes a JS string as JSON text with quotes. The snippets return numbers (`bytesWritten`, `files.length`), thus the test compares the output text to `String(count)` with no decoder.
+    - `FileChangeEventAbsenceTests` has a private `writeSnippet`. The new suite needs the same snippet with a file name parameter. A shared `writeVerbSnippet(writing:content:)` in `FilesRunFixtures.swift` replaces both copies.
